title: Introduce contrast modes and dynamic radius tokens for collapsible cards
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Collapsible card components render inconsistently across density modes and struggle with text/background contrast when nested in dense tables or overlays. Goal: Add two token families: contrast-modes (default, high-contrast, muted) and radius-dynamic (fluid values keyed to component density). Deliver a migration path so existing card components use the new tokens without visual regressions and meet WCAG AA for body/label combinations. Scope includes token definitions, Figma comps, token implementation in the token repo, component updates (cards + nested table rows), visual regression baselines, and rollout documentation.
tasks: Produce Figma variants: default / high-contrast / muted across compact and spacious densities for Card, CollapsibleCard, and NestedCard-in-Table
Update tokens repo: add entries and migration notes (tokens.json + changelog)
Engineering: implement token hooks in Card component, add theme toggles for contrast modes
Create migration script to map legacy tokens and generate a fallback map for older deployments
Add visual regression tests and baseline images; run across supported themes and densities
Accessibility audit: run contrast checker and document failing cases and fixes
Docs: write rollout guide, example usage, and API notes for token overrides
Release checklist and coordinate with Console engineering for feature flag rollout
acceptance_criteria: New token families (contrast-modes and radius-dynamic) merged to tokens repo with examples
Card components use new tokens by default and preserve current visual appearance in default theme
High-contrast mode meets WCAG AA for body text against its background in all densities
Migration script maps >95% of legacy token usages and creates safe fallbacks for remaining cases
Visual regressions reviewed and approved; any intentional diffs documented
Design docs and Figma files linked in the tokens repo; rollout guide published
Feature flag exists to toggle contrast-modes in production for gradual rollout
